source.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Generalize? A Case Study of Answerability
source.authors: Lovis Heindrich; P. Torr; Fazl Barez; Veronika Thost

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE features capture answerability across datasets and finds their generalization inconsistent, refining the scope of claims about SAE features as general representations. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The study tests answerability detection with SAE features and compares it with residual-stream probes. Results cited from prior work are not included. Fine-grained values visible only in plots are not estimated.
record.test_reason: The study checks whether Gemma Scope SAE latents for one abstract concept (answerability) transfer across datasets, layers and prompts. It finds no fully general feature, with transfer ranging from near random to beating residual probes. This bears on V5 (SAE features as complete, canonical units) and weakly on V4 (whether an SAE recovers a sparse answerability feature at all). It does not touch toy-model superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say fully general features might not be learned by standard SAE training, possibly because of suboptimal objectives and feature splitting. They call comprehensive out-of-distribution evaluation critical before SAEs are robust in practice.
record.recipe_differences: This is an LLM SAE-feature probing and generalization study, not a toy-network superposition experiment or reproduction of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization varies with evaluation dataset and layer. The paper says changing the training dataset can make transfer considerably worse. It reports that small prompt-template variations do not substantially affect performance, and that post-activation sampling reduces the number of relevant features found without changing the overall result.
record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2025 Workshop on Reliable and Responsible Foundation Models
record.problems: Evidence is limited to Gemma 2 for the main evaluation, with only preliminary Llama testing. The paper notes dependence on SAE training hyperparameters and data, and uses simple feature-search/probe methods. Many fine-grained results are presented in figures without exact values stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Did not transcribe individual feature bars, seed-level values, or further per-dataset/per-layer figure-only readings from Figures 6–15 and Appendix analyses where the text gives no distinct result beyond the summarized findings. Base-model results are not separated by named checkpoint; the paper only gives a general statement that performance was relatively low.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
All: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
Whether features are distributed across neurons; recoverability beyond answerability.
Stability across SAE training runs, widths and seeds; completeness of the dictionary as a whole.
All: dimensionality of features not examined.

missing.what: Top answerability SAE features are highly dissimilar to each other and to residual probes; residual probes across seeds average cosine 0.7. Averaging features increases similarity to probes.
Good layer-20 features exist for BoolQ, Equation and Celebrity, but they are not the features selected on SQUAD.
Probes trained on BoolQ generalize considerably worse to the other datasets.
Post-activation sampling finds fewer relevant features but leaves the overall results unchanged.

record.verdict_notes: The study relies on Gemma Scope SAEs and tests them only through 1-sparse probing. Its bearing on superposition is indirect, via V4 and V5. Model size is not stated; layers 20/31 and 131k width suggest Gemma 2 9B IT. Most values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions are not tested.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not test polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
It tests SAE-feature answerability detection and transfer, not whether features are spread across neurons or how often features are recoverable for other concepts.
It tests answerability generalization across datasets, but not feature stability across SAE training runs or whether SAE features are canonical units for the model generally.
The dimensionality of represented features is not tested.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Fit a 1-sparse SAE-feature answerability probe using SQUAD data.
rows.note: The paper reports this for the best SAE features.
rows.check: The value is the best of selected features (around 0.8). Model size is not stated, though layers 20/31 and 131k width imply Gemma 2 9B IT.

source_check.correct: Best layer-31 SAE features: accuracy around 0.8; residual-stream linear probes: accuracy 0.9.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Linear vs SAE Probes: Generalization, Figure 3 discussion.
source_check.problem: The text states a residual-stream probe baseline; baseline not stated omits it.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Train a linear probe on the residual stream using SQUAD data.
rows.note: The paper says the residual-stream probe performs better in-domain than the best SAE features.
rows.check: Residual-stream linear probe comparator; it measures no SAE feature, so it should not link to V4.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on SQUAD on the Equation dataset.
rows.baseline: Residual-stream linear probe; exact value not stated
rows.value: The best SAE features generalize better than the residual-stream probe; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The paper limits this result to layer 31 features trained on SQUAD and says layer 20 performs considerably worse.
rows.check: Cross-dataset transfer measures generality of the unit, not recoverability, so drop V4. Holds only for top layer-31 features trained on SQUAD.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Equation generalization discussion accompanying Figure 3.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on SQUAD on IDK data.
rows.baseline: Residual-stream linear probe; exact value not stated
rows.value: Some, but few, top SAE features match the linear probe; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper describes the matching performance as applying to only a few top features.
rows.check: Drop V4; transfer is a V5 question. Only a few top features match the probe.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Figure 3 discussion of IDK and Celebrity.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on SQUAD on Celebrity data.
rows.baseline: Residual-stream linear probe; exact value not stated
rows.value: Some, but few, top SAE features outperform the linear probe; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper separately says the linear probe performs badly on Celebrity data.
rows.check: Drop V4. Only a few features transfer; the comparator probe itself performs badly on Celebrity.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Figure 3 discussion of IDK and Celebrity.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on SQUAD on BoolQ data.
rows.value: Almost random; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The paper describes generalization to BoolQ as considerably bad.
rows.check: Drop V4. SQUAD-selected features are near random on BoolQ.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on SQUAD on small variations of the SQUAD prompt template.
rows.baseline: Default SQUAD prompt template; exact value not stated
rows.value: The SAE features generalize well to these prompt variations; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper characterizes this as an easier OOD case than its other test datasets.
rows.check: Drop V4. Authors call this an easy out-of-distribution case; the residual probe is also insensitive.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5; Appendix B.2; Figure 10 caption and Table 3.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate SAE-feature probes trained on English SQUAD data on Spanish SQUAD data.
rows.baseline: Residual-stream probe; exact value not stated
rows.value: Top SAE probes and the residual probe generalize roughly equally well, with a performance gap of slightly below 10%.
rows.note: The paper does not state which method has the advantage in this comparison.
rows.check: Drop V4. All probes lose slightly under 10%; it is not a gap between SAE and residual probes.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.6, Spanish language generalization; Figure 15.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate combinations of multiple top SAE features as answerability probes.
rows.baseline: Best-performing individual feature; exact value not stated
rows.value: OOD performance does not improve beyond the best individual feature; exact values not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Quartile ranges are shown; exact values not stated.
rows.note: Adding features improves in-domain performance, but the paper reports no corresponding OOD improvement.
rows.check: This compares variants of the study's own probe method (number of features). It does not measure whether features are canonical units.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Train and evaluate 1-sparse SAE-feature probes separately on each contrastive dataset.
rows.value: Each dataset has a detectable feature with probing accuracy over 80%.
rows.note: These are dataset-specific train-and-evaluate results, not cross-dataset generalization results.
rows.check: Per-dataset selection shows recoverable features (over 80%). Do not link to V5 transfer.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.3, In-domain SAE feature accuracies; Figure 11 caption.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.baseline: Layer 31 results; exact values not stated
rows.value: Performance is generally worse than at layer 31; Celebrity results are significantly worse than the others for both SAE and residual-stream probes.
rows.note: The paper reports one SAE feature above random on Celebrity as an exception.
rows.check: Layer-20 transfer is a V5 generality result. Drop V4, since layer 20 still has good per-dataset features (Fig 11).

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, layer-20 discussion; Appendix B.1; Figure 7.

rows.subject: Llama instruction-tuned model
rows.operation_detail: Preliminary search for SAE answerability features with sufficient in-domain probing accuracy.
rows.measure: Availability of SAE features with sufficient probing accuracy
rows.value: The authors could not find usable answerability features for a probing comparison.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a preliminary test.
rows.check: Preliminary test with unofficial SAEs of uncertain quality; this should be stated in the row.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate best SAE features on the answerability task.
rows.note: The paper says performance on Gemma 2 2B and base models was relatively low; the approximately 70% figure is stated for the best SAE features.
rows.check: Also covers base models, which are not named. Around 70% is the best feature.

relationships.condition: Gemma 2 (9B implied) instruction-tuned, Gemma Scope SAEs, features selected per dataset
relationships.reason: Single SAE latents detect answerability at around 0.8 in-domain and over 80% per dataset (R1, R10).
relationships.display_finding: Single SAE latents detected answerability at around 0.8 in-domain and above 80% on each dataset.

relation.reason: The study directly evaluates recoverable SAE answerability features and their generality across datasets, layers and prompts.

tranche.reason: Dataset-dependent transfer and failed BoolQ generalization qualify V5's account of stable, canonical dictionary units.

source_check.notes: The main Gemma 2 model size is unstated. Transfer failures test operational feature generality; they do not establish absence of a complete dictionary or directly test cross-seed canonical identity.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Dataset-specific detection and selected transfer settings
reader_labels.reason: SAE features detect answerability above 80% when trained and evaluated per dataset, and some transfer results are positive, including Equation and prompt variations (R3, R5, R7, R10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-dataset transfer, layer choice, and the preliminary Llama test
reader_labels.reason: Transfer is uneven: it is weak on BoolQ, only a few features match or exceed the comparator on IDK and Celebrity, layer 20 is generally worse, and usable features were not found in the preliminary Llama test (R4, R6, R11, R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Answerability generalization across tested datasets and feature combinations
reader_labels.reason: Some features transfer, but transfer is inconsistent and combining features does not improve OOD performance beyond the best individual feature; this supports only a limited, task- and dataset-dependent account, not complete or canonical units generally (R3-R6, R9).
